drivingQuestion: When a primary food is eaten together with a secondary one, over which is the blessing recited?
outcomeNote: A mishna stating a rule and its generalising principle; no dispute and no dialectic within the unit.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הֵבִיאוּ לְפָנָיו מָלִיחַ תְּחִלָּה וּפַת עִמּוֹ — מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַמָּלִיחַ וּפוֹטֵר אֶת הַפַּת, שֶׁהַפַּת טְפֵלָה לוֹ. זֶה הַכְּלָל: כׇּל שֶׁהוּא עִיקָּר וְעִמּוֹ טְפֵלָה — מְבָרֵךְ עַל הָעִיקָּר וּפוֹטֵר אֶת הַטְּפֵלָה.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» If «they brought salted» food «before him» to eat «first and bread with it, he recites a blessing over the salted» food «and» thereby «exempts the bread, because» the salted food is primary while «the bread is secondary to it. This is the principle: Any» food «that is primary and a secondary» food «is with it, one recites a blessing over the primary and,» in so doing, «exempts the secondary» from its own blessing.

moves.cueHe: הביאו לפניו מליח תחלה ופת עמו
moves.summary: one served salted food first with bread alongside it blesses the salted food and so exempts the bread
moves.about: the mishna generalises its own salted-food ruling into a principle covering any primary food accompanied by a secondary one

moves.summary: the case is generalised: wherever there is a primary food and a secondary one with it, the blessing on the primary exempts the secondary

edges.cueHe: זה הכלל: כל שהוא עיקר ועמו טפלה
edges.about: the mishna generalises its own salted-food ruling into a principle covering any primary food accompanied by a secondary one
